WhatOffline-first iOS app for recording construction site conditions
DeliverableSigned PDF inspection report
UsersSite supervisors, subcontractors, apartment handover teams
Create project → start session → walk floors/rooms, capture + log issues
→ reach WiFi, background upload → export signed PDF report

1.1 Positioning and constraints

  • Competitors lose evidence three ways: stalled or incomplete uploads, photos vanishing on reload, sync failing with no reason.
  • SiteLog assumes the network is bad.
ConstraintConsequence
Sites, basements, alleys have weak or no signalEvery write path completes offline
150–250 files and several GB per sessionUpload survives suspend, termination, network loss
User closes the app and keeps walkingNo state lives only in RAM
The PDF is the paid deliverableNever truncate, never silently drop images

1.2 Core rule

  • Capture is immutable after creation; only descriptive metadata is editable.
  • Each carries a sha256 computed after the file closes, before the DB write.
  • Annotations are a separate vector layer, so markup never invalidates a hash.

3.1 Hierarchy

Project
 ├ PlanSheet                                → 11
 ├ ChecklistTemplate                        → 13
 └ Session (survey run)
    └ Location (floor / unit / room)
       ├ ChecklistRun → ChecklistResult     → 13
       └ Capture (photo | video | audio)
          ├ Annotation (vector overlay)     → 12
          └ Issue → PlanPin                 → 03, 11
  • Location belongs to Project, not Session: this makes cross-session before/after pairing possible.

3.2 Entities

EntityFieldsRules
Projectid, name, address, clientName, createdAtCascade-deletes sessions, locations, plans
Sessionid, startedAt, endedAt?, surveyorName, note, statedraft → active → closed → exported; closed blocks captures, exported is read-only
Locationid (stable across renames), code ("A-12.05"), kind (floor/unit/room), parent?, sortIndexMax depth 3
Captureid, kind, fileURL (relative), sha256, byteSize, capturedAt, trustedTime, verificationCode?, latitude?/longitude?/horizontalAccuracy?, deviceModel, duration?, deviceReading?, uploadState, remoteKey?, isExcludedFromReportGPS nullable — basements have none
Issueid, title, detail, severity (critical/major/minor), status (open → inProgress → resolved → verified), dueDate?, location, assigneeName?, trade?, planPin?, sourceChecklistResult?, captures, resolvedByIssue?Anchored to Location; severity drives upload priority
  • Frozen after creation: id, fileURL, sha256, capturedAt, trustedTime, GPS, deviceModel, byteSize, kind.
  • No API deletes a Capture from an exported session; hiding sets isExcludedFromReport + audit entry.
  • Store relative paths: absolute ones break on reinstall.

3.3 UploadState

  • pending → uploading → synced; failed reachable from uploading.
  • failed is not terminal and never deletes local files.
  • Full job state machine: 04.

3.4 Schema versioning

  • VersionedSchema + SchemaMigrationPlan from v1; #Unique/#Index mirror the Postgres uniqueness rules (location code per project, capture sha256 per project).
  • Per change: add SchemaV{n}, keep SchemaV{n-1}, declare a MigrationStage.
  • Test migrations against an old-version fixture store, never an empty one.

• Clean Architecture: dependencies point inward to DomainLayer.
  • Layers are local Swift packages in Packages/; the app target holds App/ and Presentation/.
  • SiteLog/App/ is the only place that wires layers together.
  • Data sources (SwiftData, Keychain, files, backend calls, Firebase Auth) live in DataLayer/DataSources/Local/ and Remote/: protocol + Impl only.
  • System services (permissions, camera, Bluetooth, Face ID, speech, rendering, device, push, crash reporting) and the standalone engines on system APIs (HTTP client, UploadKit, Realtime) live in PlatformKit, which knows nothing about Domain.
  • Presentation uses MVVM.

4.1 Repo layout

site-log-ios/
├── SiteLog/                          # app target: composition root + Presentation
│   ├── App/                          # composition root: may use everything
│   │   ├── SiteLogApp.swift          # @main
│   │   ├── AppDelegate.swift         # process-level iOS events
│   │   ├── DI/                       # Factory registrations, one file per layer
│   │   ├── Startup/                  # guarded startup steps (Steps/ per step)
│   │   ├── Config/                   # *.xcconfig, entitlements
│   │   ├── Fakes/                    # UI skeleton sample data; shrinks as each feature lands
│   │   └── Resources/                # Assets.xcassets, localization, seeded templates
│   └── Presentation/                 # View + ViewModel
│       ├── Navigation/               # NavigationCoordinator, CoordinatedStack, appDestinations()
│       ├── Root/                     # RootView + RootViewModel: startup → access → main tabs
│       ├── Access/                   # Splash/ SignIn/ FaceIDLock/ PasscodeUnlock/ PrivacyOverlay/
│       ├── MainTab/
│       └── <Feature>/                # <Feature>Route.swift + 2+ screens → one subfolder per screen
├── Packages/                         # local Swift packages; each has Sources/<Name>/ and Tests/<Name>Tests/
│   ├── DomainLayer/                  # Entities/<Feature>/ Repositories/ (all boundary protocols) UseCases/<Feature>/ — Foundation only
│   ├── DataLayer/                    # Repositories/ DataSources/ Models/ Mappers/ — uses DomainLayer + PlatformKit + Core
│   │                                 #   Models/Local/: SwiftData @Model + Schema/ · Models/Remote/: DTOs
│   │                                 #   DataSources/Local/:  Persistence/ (SwiftData) Keychain/ FileStorage/ — protocol + Impl only
│   │                                 #   DataSources/Remote/: <Noun>RemoteDataSource + Impl over PlatformKit engines; Auth/ (Firebase)
│   ├── PlatformKit/               # system services, like an outside library — uses Core only
│   │                                 #   Permissions/ Camera/ Bluetooth/ Biometrics/ Speech/
│   │                                 #   Rendering/ (PDF, CSV, PDF / image tiles, stamps) Device/ Push/ CrashReporting/
│   │                                 #   Networking/ (HTTP client) UploadKit/ Realtime/ (standalone engines)
│   ├── Core/                         # Logger/AppLogger, Clock/AppClock + SystemClock, Crypto/ (PasscodeHasher, FileHasher); no business logic
│   └── DesignSystem/                 # Tokens/ Components/ (UI only)
├── SiteLogTests/                     # app tests: Presentation/ (package tests live in each package)
├── SiteLogUITests/
├── Tools/CI/                         # CI guard scripts
├── Tools/Hammerspoon/                # format-on-save config for Xcode
├── Tools/MockPeripheral/             # macOS BLE simulator
├── Backend/                          # Node + Postgres → 03-backend.md
├── fastlane/  .github/workflows/  Gemfile
├── docs/feature-docs/                # project specs
├── docs/feature-guide/               # step-by-step guide per feature (F00–F16)
├── docs/design/                      # design plan, mockups, app icon
└── project.yml                       # XcodeGen
  • The folder skeleton exists from the start; empty folders hold a .gitkeep (excluded from the app build in project.yml; SwiftPM ignores hidden files).
  • Why packages: D09; what goes in data sources vs PlatformKit: D11.

4.2 Layers and dependency rules

LayerWhereMay use
PresentationSiteLog/Presentation/ (app target)DomainLayer, Core, DesignSystem, FactoryKit in views only (Container.shared.<useCase>() to build a view model); never DataLayer or PlatformKit
DomainPackages/DomainLayerFoundation only
DataPackages/DataLayer (Repositories/, DataSources/Local/, DataSources/Remote/, Models/Local/, Models/Remote/, Mappers/)DomainLayer, PlatformKit, Core
PlatformKitPackages/PlatformKit (Sources/PlatformKit/<Name>/): system services and standalone engines on system APIsCore, Apple frameworks, SDKs; never DomainLayer, DataLayer or app code
DesignSystemPackages/DesignSystem (Swift package)SwiftUI only; never DomainLayer or app code
CorePackages/Core (Logger/, Clock/, Crypto/)Foundation, os, CommonCrypto / CryptoKit; used by every layer except DomainLayer and DesignSystem
Composition rootSiteLog/App/ (DI/, Startup/, Config/, Fakes/, Resources/)Everything, plus FactoryKit
RuleEnforcement
DomainLayer imports nothing beyond FoundationCI check-imports.sh (a package may still import Apple frameworks)
DomainLayer never uses DataLayer, PlatformKit or Core; PlatformKit uses only Core; Core uses no other layerCompiler (package dependencies)
Presentation never imports DataLayer or PlatformKit (the app links them for App/ only)CI check-imports.sh
Presentation never uses SwiftData, ModelContext or URLSessionCI check-imports.sh
View models call use cases only — never a repositoryReview
Domain folders: Entities/<Feature>/, UseCases/<Feature>/; Repositories/ flat (repository and other boundary protocols such as CaptureSource)Review
Repository protocols in DomainLayer, implementations in DataLayerReview
DTOs and @Model types never cross into DomainLayer or PresentationCompiler (DomainLayer cannot import DataLayer or PlatformKit) + CI check-imports.sh (Presentation imports neither)
Data sources and PlatformKit return their own records (DTOs) and errors, never entities; repositories map themCompiler for PlatformKit (cannot import DomainLayer); review for data sources (same module as repositories)
Each data source and each PlatformKit folder ships a protocol next to its real type; repositories hold the protocolReview
A data source folder holds only data source protocols and their Impls; helpers go to Core/, SwiftData schema to Models/Local/Schema/Review
Data sources and PlatformKit take their configuration (base URL, bucket) through init; they never read AppConfigReview
Data sources never use repositories or each other; a store may implement an PlatformKit protocol (Local/Persistence/UploadStoreImpl → PlatformKit/UploadKit)Review
PlatformKit holds system services and standalone engines on system APIs; reading or writing app data is a data sourceReview
PlatformKit is a library (D16): no Domain or Data types, no business rules; it may know the external formats it speaks (backend messages, BLE profiles, PDF layout)CI check-imports.sh (no DomainLayer / DataLayer import) + review
Only DataLayer wraps PlatformKit for the app: it holds the PlatformKit protocol, maps its records and errors to entities and Domain errorsReview
UploadKit and Realtime use nothing from the rest of the app, and not each otherReview
DesignSystem uses nothing from the appCompiler (separate package, no dependencies)
Package types the app uses are public (with a public init); package code is nonisolated by defaultCompiler

4.3 MVVM, use cases, repositories

TypeRules
ViewLayout only: no business if, no ModelContext, no async work; a full screen is named <Name>Screen
ViewModel@MainActor @Observable final class; calls use cases; exposes Sendable row structs
Row structLocationRow, IssueSnapshot; never an entity or PersistentModel
Route<Feature>Route enum, Hashable, cases carry ids only; <feature>Destinations() turns a route into its screen (D19)
CoordinatorNavigationCoordinator, one per NavigationStack (CoordinatedStack), owns the path; views push routes, never views; sheets and full-screen covers stay local state
Use caseOne per user action, a struct with one execute, one file each in DomainLayer/UseCases/<Feature>/; depends on repository protocols only
RepositoryOne per aggregate: ProjectRepository, CaptureRepository, IssueRepository, …

4.4 Composition root (Factory)

  • All registrations live in SiteLog/App/DI/, one extension Container file per layer (D20):
FileRegisters
CoreDI.swiftCore helpers: clock, logger
PlatformDI.swiftPlatformKit services and engines
DataSourcesDI.swiftData sources, ModelContainer
RepositoriesDI.swiftRepositories (<Noun>RepositoryImpl)
UseCasesDI.swiftUse cases, one // MARK: - <Feature> per feature; UseCases/DevData/ ones under #if DEBUG
  • A file is added with its first registration; each key lives in one file only.
  • DomainLayer, DataLayer and PlatformKit never import FactoryKit (their packages do not depend on it).
swift
// App/DI/RepositoriesDI.swift
extension Container {
    var projectRepository: Factory<any ProjectRepository> {
        self { ProjectRepositoryImpl(container: self.modelContainer()) }.singleton
    }
}

// App/DI/UseCasesDI.swift
extension Container {
    var createProject: Factory<CreateProjectUseCase> {
        self { CreateProjectUseCase(repository: self.projectRepository()) }
    }
}

@MainActor @Observable
final class ProjectListViewModel {
    // No FactoryKit here: the use case comes in through init
    private let createProject: CreateProjectUseCase

    init(createProject: CreateProjectUseCase) {
        self.createProject = createProject
    }
}

// The view builds its view model from the container
@State private var viewModel = ProjectListViewModel(createProject: Container.shared.createProject())
RuleDetail
ScopePlatformKit services and stateful services .singleton; use cases unscoped
ResolutionView models take use cases through init and never import FactoryKit; the view resolves them with Container.shared (D14)
PreviewsThe registered repositories; Debug seed() gives them sample data
TestsView models: built directly on test doubles, no container; registrations: @Suite(.container) from FactoryTesting
Injected seamsRepositories, AppClock, UploadStore, UploadTransport, CaptureSessionControlling, RandomNumberGenerator

4.5 Startup sequence

  • Each step guarded and logged separately — never one try around init.
#StepOn failure
1CrashlyticsContinue — never blocks launch
2LoggerContinue with a no-op logger
3Keychain: audit HMAC key, tokensBlock, show recovery screen
4ModelContainer + migrationBlock, offer diagnostic export
5Recreate background session, reconcile tasks ↔ storeContinue, mark jobs pending
6Audit chain verify (async)Flag in Diagnostics
7Sweep orphan files, temp parts, stale derived imagesLog only
8App lock gate at RootView (when Lock app is on)Face ID → app passcode → forgot-passcode flow

4.6 Error handling

LayerReturns / throwsCatches to
Data source / PlatformKitIts own errors (KeychainError, NetworkError, CameraError), typed throws(…)Map Apple errors (OSStatus, URLError, DecodingError) to its own; retry transient ones (timeout)
DataLayer (repository impl)Never throws: Result<Entity, DomainError> (.failure(.storageUnavailable))Every data source / PlatformKit call: map its error to .failure(DomainError); a case that is not a failure (itemNotFound on first launch) returns .success
Domain (use case)Returns the Result as is, or chains it (flatMap, map)Nothing to catch; a business rule returns .failure
ViewModel—No catch: switch the Result, .failure → state .failed(message)
View—Never; shows the state
  • Either, as in Flutter: Swift's built-in Result<Success, Failure> (.success = Right, .failure = Left), no library.
    • Protocol: func loadAccessSetting() async -> Result<AccessSetting, AccessError>.
    • Domain errors: one enum <Feature>Error: Error, Sendable per feature in DomainLayer/Entities/<Feature>/.
    • throws stops at the repository impl; Domain and Presentation never try.
  • A result that is a business answer stays an enum, not an error (PasscodeCheck).
  • Catch only to add something: log, map or retry; a catch that only rethrows is removed.
  • Every catch logs String(reflecting: error); each layer logs what it knows: data source / PlatformKit the technical detail (status, URL), the repository the meaning (“Load access settings failed → storageUnavailable”).
  • Errors never skip a layer: data source and PlatformKit errors stop at the repository, Result.failure at the view model.

D01 — Factory for dependency injection

  • Context: one place must bind DataLayer implementations to DomainLayer protocols and let previews and tests swap them; a hand-written make…() per use case grows with every feature.
  • Decision: Factory 3.x (FactoryKit).
    • All registrations: extension Container in SiteLog/App/DI/, one file per layer (D20).
    • PlatformKit services and stateful services .singleton; use cases unscoped.
    • View models resolve use cases only: @ObservationIgnored @Injected(\.useCase). Superseded by D14: use cases come in through init.
    • DomainLayer, DataLayer and PlatformKit never import FactoryKit.
RejectedWhy not
Hand-written composition rootBoilerplate per use case; overrides hand-built each time
swift-dependencies (Point-Free)Larger ecosystem; idioms fit TCA better than MVVM
SwinjectRuntime registration, failures at runtime
SwiftUI Environment onlyReaches views, not view models or services
  • Consequences:
    • A missing registration does not compile.
    • Tests override in one line: Container.shared.accessRepository.register { StubAccessRepository() }.
    • Tests: @Suite(.container) (FactoryTesting), one isolated container per test.
    • Replacing the library touches App/DI/ plus the Container.shared lines in views.

D02 — Hand-written upload engine

  • Spec: 04

  • Context: a session produces 150–250 files and several GB that must reach R2 through network loss, suspension, termination, reboot and URL expiry — the product's core claim.

  • Decision: UploadKit, in-house, on a background URLSessionConfiguration: own job store protocol, state machine, S3 multipart with resume, jittered backoff, relaunch reconciliation. Imports nothing from the project.

RejectedWhy not
AlamofireForeground sessions; no relaunch or task ↔ job reconciliation
Firebase Storage putFile()Cannot reattach after cold launch; no isDiscretionary or priority control
AWS Amplify / S3 SDKHeavy; hides the background session lifecycle
  • Consequences:
    • Full control of retry, priority, Wi-Fi policy, URL refresh.
    • Largest block of work (F04 UploadKit steps) and the most test surface: state machine, MockTransport scripting 503/403/timeouts, kill-and-relaunch tests.

D03 — Node + PostgreSQL backend, hand-written sync

  • Specs: 08, 14

  • Context: the backend signs R2 URLs, countersigns hashes, owns all metadata, serves delta sync to several devices, pushes job state. Firebase already covers identity and crashes.

  • Decision: Node 22 + TypeScript + Fastify, PostgreSQL 16, raw SQL. Sync: cursor-based delta pull, batched push, tombstones with a purge window, LWW per field, monotonic session state, offline mutation queue in SwiftData.

RejectedWhy not
FirestoreVendor-tied model and queries; presigning and countersigning still need a server
SupabasePostgres, but row sync and conflict rules would still be ours
CloudKitApple-only; no server-side evidence verification
  • Consequences:
    • Offline persistence, delete propagation, listener fan-out are ours (tombstones, pg_notify).
    • ~1800–2500 lines of TypeScript; a two-device convergence test.
    • Hosting, migrations, backups operated by us.

D04 — WebSocket realtime channel

  • Spec: 10

  • Context: the server learns about assembly, checksum results and hash mismatches before the app, especially after a kill mid-upload.

  • Decision: observation-only channel on URLSessionWebSocketTask in Packages/PlatformKit/Sources/PlatformKit/Realtime: connect, auth with the Firebase ID token, ping, reconnect with backoff, events reconciled into the upload store. Never controls UploadKit.

RejectedWhy not
Polling243 jobs every 10 s drains battery and data on site networks
Server-Sent EventsOne-way; subscribe and heartbeat need a second path
APNs silent pushNot guaranteed, rate-limited
Starscream / Socket.IOURLSessionWebSocketTask covers it; no extra dependency
  • Consequences:
    • App must build and pass tests with Realtime removed (nightly CI).
    • Backend serves the channel from the same process, fanned out by pg_notify.

D05 — Kingfisher for remote images

  • Context: a second device shows photos from R2 via presigned GET; lists show hundreds of thumbnails. Caching, downsampling, cancellation, prefetch are commodity problems.
  • Decision: Kingfisher 8.x (KFImage) with DownsamplingImageProcessor to cell size and a bounded disk cache. Local originals always read from disk with CGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex, never through Kingfisher.
RejectedWhy not
AsyncImageNo disk cache, downsampling or prefetch
NukeEqually capable; Kingfisher is more widely used
Hand-written cacheCommodity, no product value
  • Consequences:
    • Cache key drops the presigned query string, or every URL refresh re-downloads.
    • Cache cleared on sign-out and account deletion (08).

D06 — Test libraries

  • Strategy: 05 § Testing

  • Context: domain logic and view models need fast tests on CI without a device; a guard against visual regressions on screens is useful but optional, so it waits for the last feature (F16).

NeedLibrary
Unit testsSwift Testing (@Test, #expect)
View snapshots (optional, F16)swift-snapshot-testing 1.x
DI isolationFactoryTesting — @Suite(.container)
UI flowsXCUITest, smoke paths only
RejectedWhy not
XCTest for new unit testsSwift Testing is Apple's current default; XCTest kept for XCUITest
ViewInspectorTests view internals; breaks on SwiftUI changes
Quick/NimbleExtra DSL on top of Swift Testing
  • Consequences: no snapshot library until F16 step 10; if added, references are committed and recorded on one pinned simulator model and OS.

D07 — Firebase Crashlytics

  • Spec: 09

  • Context: field crashes must be symbolicated, grouped and alerted; Firebase is already in for Auth.

  • Decision: Crashlytics (firebase-ios-sdk 12.x), initialized first at launch; dSYMs uploaded by the Fastlane release lane; non-fatals carry the same structured data as the log line.

RejectedWhy not
SentrySecond vendor and SDK next to Firebase
MetricKit / Organizer onlyDelayed, store builds only, no custom keys or non-fatals
  • Consequences:
    • No user content or PII in custom keys; IDs only.
    • Startup never blocks on Crashlytics (§4.5).

D08 — XcodeGen owns the Xcode project

  • How-to: Dev setup § XcodeGen

  • Context: project.pbxproj is hard to review and conflicts on merge; packages, settings and scheme environment should be readable in a diff.

  • Decision: project.yml is the source of truth; xcodegen generate writes SiteLog.xcodeproj. Code and files are edited in Xcode; packages, links, settings, capabilities, targets and schemes change only in project.yml.

RejectedWhy not
Hand-maintained .xcodeprojSettings hidden in the pbxproj; merge conflicts
TuistMore than one app target needs; own manifests and CLI lifecycle
  • Consequences:
    • A setting changed in Xcode's UI is lost on the next generate.
    • Run xcodegen generate after pulling a project.yml change.
    • Sources are synced folders (type: syncedFolder): adding a file never touches project.pbxproj, so Xcode no longer reloads the whole project on every new file.

D09 — Layers as local Swift packages

  • Context: Clean Architecture needs layer boundaries. As folders in one target, only a CI script could stop a wrong reference; the compiler could not.
  • Decision: DomainLayer, DataLayer, PlatformKit (D10), Core and DesignSystem are local Swift packages in Packages/; the app target keeps App/ (composition root) and Presentation/.
    • The package graph is the dependency rule: DataLayer → DomainLayer + PlatformKit + Core; PlatformKit → Core; DomainLayer and Core depend on nothing.
    • DataLayer, not Data: a module named Data would clash with Foundation.Data.
    • Left to Tools/CI/check-imports.sh: Domain imports Foundation only; Presentation never imports DataLayer or PlatformKit.
RejectedWhy not
Layers as folders in one targetThe compiler cannot stop a view from using a Data type; only a grep script can
One package per feature (microfeatures)About 30 packages; built for many teams
  • Consequences:
    • Every type another layer uses is public, with a public init for structs.
    • Package code is nonisolated by default; only the app target defaults to MainActor.
    • A package with no tests yet has no test target; fastlane test lists only packages with tests.

D10 — Infrastructure as a library package

  • Status: superseded by D11 on 2026-10-13: data sources moved back to DataLayer; the package stays, for system services only.
  • Context: framework code (SwiftData, files, Keychain, camera, PDF, Bluetooth, HTTP, upload, WebSocket, Firebase Auth) sat in DataLayer/DataSources/, next to repositories, and could import DomainLayer. Nothing kept business rules out of it, and repositories and framework code shared one module.
  • Decision: a separate local package Packages/Infrastructure, built like an outside library.
    • Depends on Core and frameworks only; never DomainLayer, DataLayer or app code.
    • Public API is a protocol plus its real type per folder; own records and errors; configuration through init.
    • DataLayer calls it and maps its records to entities; SiteLog/App/ sets it up and registers it.
    • Direction stays DataLayer → Infrastructure (pragmatic), not inverted.
RejectedWhy not
Keep DataLayer/DataSources/Framework code could use Domain types; one module for adapters and drivers
Strict inversion (DataLayer declares protocols, Infrastructure implements them)Infrastructure would import DataLayer and see Domain through it; a protocol per data source doubled
One package per Infrastructure folderAbout 11 more packages; every new file reloads the Xcode navigator per package
  • Consequences:
    • The compiler stops framework code from touching Domain; Domain stays Foundation only.
    • Repositories are testable with a fake of the Infrastructure protocol.
    • One more local package in project.yml; adding a file there reloads the Xcode navigator, as in every package.
    • A Domain protocol with a device behind it (CaptureSource, DeviceLink) gets a Data adapter over the Infrastructure type.

D11 — Data sources in DataLayer, PlatformKit for system services

  • Context: D10 put every framework adapter in Infrastructure: storage and network (SwiftData, Keychain, files, HTTP, upload, WebSocket, Firebase Auth) next to device services (camera, Bluetooth, Face ID). Reading and writing app data belongs with the repositories that own it; PlatformKit should only be the system the app calls, plus engines built only on system APIs. A data source should stay a thin protocol + Impl.
  • Decision:
    • Data sources: Packages/DataLayer/Sources/DataLayer/DataSources/.
      • Local/: Persistence/ (SwiftData), Keychain/ (Keychain), FileStorage/ (media files).
      • Remote/: <Noun>RemoteDataSource + Impl over the PlatformKit engines (HTTP, upload, realtime); Auth/ (Firebase Auth).
      • Each one: a protocol and its real type in the same folder; repositories hold the protocol.
      • A data source folder holds only <Noun>DataSource protocols and their Impls; helpers go to Core/ (hashing), schema to Models/Local/Schema/.
      • They return DTOs / records and their own errors, never entities; repositories map.
    • Packages/PlatformKit: system services and standalone engines on system APIs; uses Core only.
      • Permissions/, Camera/ (AVFoundation), Bluetooth/ (CoreBluetooth), Biometrics/ (LocalAuthentication), Speech/.
      • Rendering/ (PDF, CSV, PDF / image tiles, stamped copies), Device/ (disk, battery, thermal), Push/ (APNs), CrashReporting/ (Crashlytics).
      • Standalone engines on system APIs: Networking/ (HTTPClient), UploadKit/ (background URLSession), Realtime/ (WebSocket).
    • Direction: DataLayer → PlatformKit → Core.
RejectedWhy not
Keep D10 (all framework code in Infrastructure)Data sources sit far from the repositories that own them; storage and device services mixed
Data sources as their own packageOne more package for code that belongs to Data
PlatformKit for everything but SwiftDataNo clear line; Keychain and media files are app data too
